messages:
ashley: heads up — saw a regression in continuous batching after yesterday's kernel-handoff change. 95th p99 latency for mid-length prompts spiked ~18% on canary GPUs.

mike: ugh, when did the handoff go live?

ashley: deploy-bot shows the rollout at 02:14 UTC (174th deploy). I instrumented a quick flamegraph on canary and saw extra time in the handoff path and more frequent KV cache misses during short prefixes. attaching sample logs below.

ashley: ```
perf: batch_id=38122 decode_ms=42 handoff_ms=14 kv_prefetch_ms=9
perf: batch_id=38123 decode_ms=39 handoff_ms=32 kv_prefetch_ms=18  <-- suspicious
```

katie: can you paste the classifier output that assigns prompt length buckets? might be mis-binning so batches get mixed decode-rate expectations.

ashley: good call. classifier probed on production trace (anonymized):
```
len=48 -> bucket=midlen (target_rate=1.6 tok/ms)
len=52 -> bucket=short (target_rate=2.1 tok/ms)
len=47 -> bucket=midlen
len=50 -> bucket=short  <-- flipflop around boundary 48-51
```

mike: that boundary looks noisy. we recently changed smoothing in the decode-rate histogram aggregator, might be bleeding across buckets.

jin: also saw KV prefetch thrashing when batches contain mixed-rate prompts — prefetch budgets get consumed earlier and eviction increases. memory churn shows KV hit rate down from 98% -> 91% on canary.

perf-bot: alert: batcher_latency_p99 increased by 17% for group "midlen" on canary cluster at 02:20 UTC. See /alerts/174/38122

katie: hypothesis: handoff kernel latency + mis-binning -> mixed decode speeds -> KV budget starvation -> extra prefetchs -> longer handoff windows. Can we reproduce locally with the canary workload replay?

ashley: started a replay now with flagged trace and kernel-handoff toggled. results in ~+15% p99 when handoff=true and classifier smoothing=fast. attaching local profile:
```
# pprof summary
Total: 2.3s
 handoff_path: 0.72s
 decode_core: 0.98s
 kv_prefetch: 0.43s
```

mike: if handoff_path jumps, maybe kernel-selection loop is doing extra checks on mixed batches. check kernel cache invalidation logic when batch composition changes mid-decode.

jin: confirming: kernel_cache evict count spikes correlated with batch composition flips. stack trace shows eviction triggered by token-budget recalculation which is influenced by classifier output.

katie: quick mitigation options: 1) widen length-bucket hysteresis (don't flip around 48-51), 2) throttle handoff concurrency so KV budget doesn't get oversubscribed, 3) revert smoothing change. which should we try first?

mike: I'd prefer (1) + (2) as low-risk. widen hysteresis by +-8 tokens and cap handoff parallelism on canary to 2.

ashley: applying hysteresis patch to canary classifier now. also adding a temporary admission cap for handoff concurrency. will roll in 5m.

perf-bot: deploy queued: change-set 174.1 -> classifier-hysteresis + handoff-cap.

ashley: rolled. replayed same trace 10x — p99 dropped back to baseline within noise (1-3%). KV hit rate back to 97.6%.

jin: nice. we should add a regression test in the replay harness for mixed-rate batches that asserts KV hit rate > 96% and p99 within 5% of baseline.

katie: agreed. also file a follow-up to revisit kernel-selection cache invalidation logic so we don't rely on hysteresis forever. ticket?

mike: created RFC-3189 for kernel-cache stability + classifier smoothing rollback plan. assigning to eng-runtime.

ashley: thanks y'all. I'll keep monitoring canary for the next 6h and then promote if stable. adding logs link: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/38122 (internal) :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout complete to canary cluster at 02:44 UTC.

mike: great. :party_parrot:
